title: Microsoft Purview: adaptive scope lifecycle status controls for recipients and site owners (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: The roadmap facts and existing scope controls are supported, and searches found no documentation for the planned lifecycle setting or its default. The policy coverage explanation needs a qualification: communication compliance does not support SharePoint sites or OneDrive accounts.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: An adaptive scope is a dynamic membership query with three scope types: Users, SharePoint sites and Microsoft 365 Groups.
claims.quote: An adaptive scope uses a query that you specify ... There are three different types of adaptive scopes ... Users ... SharePoint sites ... Microsoft 365 Groups

claims.where: What's changing: first paragraph; Why it matters: first paragraph
claims.claim: Communication compliance, retention and auto-labeling policies can target the described adaptive sets of users, groups or sites, without a policy-specific qualification.
claims.quote: For communication compliance policies: SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts aren't supported. Excluded users and Microsoft 365 groups are supported.
claims.fix: Add immediately after the adaptive scope definition: 'For communication compliance policies, SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts are not supported.' In Why it matters, replace the first sentence with: 'Changing scope membership can change policy coverage; communication compliance policies do not support SharePoint sites or OneDrive accounts.' Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-adaptive-scopes.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: No admin UI or PowerShell lifecycle-evaluation setting is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview adaptive scopes lifecycle status recipient site owner evaluation control default licensing PowerShell'; opened Adaptive scopes, New-AdaptiveScope and Set-AdaptiveScope. No lifecycle setting or parameter was found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the new control's default or whether existing scopes change on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: '"adaptive scopes" "lifecycle" "default"'; read the roadmap record, Adaptive scopes and New-AdaptiveScope. No lifecycle-control default or existing-scope rollout behaviour was stated.

claims.where: What's changing: third paragraph
claims.claim: The roadmap description does not name lifecycle states, a default or the setting's location.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Adaptive Scopes will provide administrators with explicit control over lifecycle-state evaluation for recipients and site owners, helping ensure policy targeting and scope membership remain aligned with organizational requirements.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The advanced query builder uses the OPATH property IsInactiveMailbox to exclude or target inactive mailboxes.
claims.quote: You must use the advanced query builder if you want to exclude inactive mailboxes. Or conversely, target just inactive mailboxes. For this configuration, use the OPATH property IsInactiveMailbox

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Creating an adaptive scope requires a role group with the Scope Manager role.
claims.quote: You need to assign the correct role groups to admins to create an adaptive scope. Any role group with the Scope Manager role can create an adaptive scope.

claims.where: Scope: second paragraph
claims.claim: The six named built-in role groups include Scope Manager.
claims.quote: The Scope Manger role is included in the following built-in role groups: Compliance Administrator; Compliance Data Administrator; Organization Management; Records Management; Communication Compliance; Communication Compliance Admins

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Keep Full directory when not restricting scope membership by administrative unit.
claims.quote: If you don't want to restrict the adaptive scope by using administrative units, or your organization hasn't configured administrative units, keep the default of Full directory.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The Purview portal route is Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > + Create scope > administrative unit > scope type > Advanced query builder.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes ... select + Create scope ... first asked to assign an administrative unit ... Select the type of scope ... Alternatively, you can select Advanced query builder

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: New-AdaptiveScope -Name <String> -LocationType User -RawQuery <String> creates a user scope using an advanced OPATH query.
claims.quote: New-AdaptiveScope -Name <String> -LocationType <DynamicBoundaryLocationType> -RawQuery <String> ... Valid values are: User ... The RawQuery parameter switches the scope to advanced query mode. You use OPATH filter syntax for advanced query mode.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The Purview portal membership route is Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > scope > Details > Scope details.
claims.quote: Select Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes. Select an existing adaptive scope from the list. From the Details flyout pane, select Scope details.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers -Identity <scope name> -State Removed retrieves former members of the named scope.
claims.quote: Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers -Identity "US Finance Users" -State Removed ... This example retrieves the past members of the adaptive scope US Finance Users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[2].governs; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Scope details State column shows Added for current members and Removed for members that no longer match the query.
claims.quote: Review the State column in the list that shows Added for members within the adaptive scope or Removed if the member was previously in the adaptive scope but removed now they no longer match the scope query.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Existing adaptive scope queries run daily.
claims.quote: These dynamic queries run daily against the attributes or properties that you specify for the selected scope.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Existing adaptive scope queries and changes can take up to five days to populate.
claims.quote: It can take up to five days for the queries to fully populate and changes aren't immediate. Factor in this delay by waiting a few days before you add a newly created scope to a policy.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The member details list can take up to five days to reflect added or removed members.
claims.quote: It might take up to five days for the member details list to update added or removed members.

claims.where: Why it matters: first paragraph
claims.claim: Learn says users returned by scope-validation queries without a valid adaptive-scope licence do not have policy settings applied.
claims.quote: if the number of recipients returned is higher than expected, it might be because it includes users who don't have a valid license for adaptive scopes. These users don't have the policy settings applied to them.
